newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gas demand seen at 24-year high in 1997 - IPAA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gas demand seen at 24-year high in 1997 - IPAA.

text.p: Natural gas demand in the United States is seen rising in 1997 to its highest level in 24 years, the Independent Petroleum Association of America (IPAA) told a news briefing here Wednesday.

The IPAA, which represents independent U.S. oil and gas producers, said in its short-term energy outlook that domestic natural gas consumption would rise 0.7 percent to 22.14 trillion cubic feet (TCF) this year.
This would be the first time since 1973 that gas output topped 22.0 TCF, the group said.
IPAA also forecast a 0.5 percent rise in domestic gas production this year to 19.3 TCF.
"High injection levels and demand growth are the main reasons for the expected rising production figure," the report said.
Over the longer-term, the group predicted domestic gas output would increase at an annual average rate of 1.9 percent through the year 2000 and 1.7 percent through 2010.
Total gas imports, mainly from Canada, are seen reaching 3.4 TCF by 2000, up from 2.7 TCF in 1996.
Some 4.0 TCF, or just over 14 pct of U.S. gas demand, is expected to be met by imports by the year 2010, the IPAA said.
